svg.text: HOW TO MAKE IT AND HOW IT FITS

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Cut twelve lengths of 876 mm from four 10 ft pipes (three per pipe).

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Thread one end 3/4 in NPT (rented pipe threader); ream and deburr.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Clean off cutting oil with degreaser: oil smokes on first heat.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Coat the thread with nickel anti-seize (no PTFE tape or paste) and

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: screw on the cap hand tight plus one and a half turns.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The open top end is square cut and deburred so a heater slides in.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Fit: the cap stands on a levelled 14 mm first lift of sand; the template

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: and then the lid hold the top, which ends 25 mm above the lid.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Each 508 mm heater rests on the cap inside, its heated part 26 to

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 483 mm above the drum floor; its leads rise out of the open top.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Check: length 876 mm plus cap, within 3 mm; a 16 mm rod slides
